A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ASTRA despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViT/GPT2 accuracy and perplexity results, distributed-inference latency measurements, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Llama-3-8B results, downstream evaluations, network robustness tests, heterogeneous token allocations, and repeated-seed experiments.

M1.justification: The core mixed-precision attention, noise augmentation, commitment loss, and distributed class tokens remain unchanged. v2 adds a heterogeneous-deployment adaptation using randomized unequal token allocations during training and larger token shares for stronger devices, extending v1's evenly partitioned procedure (Section 4.2 and Appendix D).

E1.justification: v2 retains CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, Wikipedia, and Wikitext-103, and adds downstream evaluations on CoLA, SST2, AG News, and QQP. It also evaluates distinct deployment scenarios involving heterogeneous token allocations, packet loss, and dynamically varying bandwidth.

E2.justification: The original single-device, TP/Megatron-LM, SP/Voltage, and BP/DeTransformer comparisons remain. Section 4.4 adds standalone post-training-quantized ViT-Base as an evaluated alternative, comparing quantization alone against quantization combined with ASTRA. The newly discussed KV-cache compression methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Existing ViT/GPT2 training budgets are retained. New protocols include 4-/8-bit quantization tests, 8-bit Llama-3-8B evaluation on TitanX GPUs, random token allocations with FPAR-based evaluation bins, 5% packet loss without retransmission, and throughput over a synthetic 600-second bandwidth trace. Appendix F also introduces a codebook-size sweep from 256 to 2048.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of quantization compatibility, accuracy versus allocation heterogeneity, resilience to packet loss and fluctuating bandwidth, codebook-size sensitivity, and memory costs. The original noise-magnitude, distributed-class-token, and commitment-loss ablations are retained in Appendix F as Tables 12–14, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 first reports ImageNet accuracy means and standard deviations across ten seeds, 0–9, and specifies seed 42 for the main experiments. Conversely, v1's statement that latency results average 20 runs disappears. The new accuracy repetitions should not be interpreted as an increase or decrease in the earlier latency-run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ImageNet accuracies for G=1/16/32 from 77.12/78.46/80.05 to 77.39/78.80/80.28; CIFAR and GPT2 entries remain unchanged. Substantial new results cover quantization, Llama, downstream tasks, heterogeneity, uncertainty, network robustness, and codebook sensitivity. These additions concern new experimental conditions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The two central theorems and their existing arguments are retained. Appendix C adds a high-rate quantization-error bound proportional to K^(-2/d) and connects it to attention error. Appendices D and G additionally define FPAR, derive its relationship to allocation variance, and derive codebook/KV-cache memory formulas.

C1.justification: The original communication-efficiency claims and headline speedups remain. v2's abstract additionally claims robustness on Llama-3-8B under packet loss and dynamic networks, while the introduction adds explicit claims about heterogeneous deployment and acceleration combined with model quantization. These materially broaden the claimed applicability.

C2.justification: New discussion explicitly limits generative acceleration to prefill, clarifying an operation already described in v1. It newly explains adaptation requirements for different device counts, distinguishes bandwidth changes from retraining needs, and discusses quantization-kernel overhead. Appendix D also interprets the relationship between allocation imbalance, full-precision attention, and accuracy. Existing zero-shot generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds Llama deployment hardware, a 52 GPU-hour adaptation cost, synthetic bandwidth-generation details, and explicit cache/codebook storage parameters. The existing optimizer and epoch information is relocated to Appendix D. Conversely, v1's open-source statement and repository URL are removed; this does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds positioning relative to KVQuant, CacheGen, and Eigen Attention, explaining their different objectives and exclusion from the main baseline set. Citations also expand for Llama, downstream datasets, network simulation, and quantization theory. The existing distributed-inference positioning and Appendix A survey are largely retained.

P1.justification: v2 renames the paper, rewrites the abstract, streamlines portions of the exposition, updates author information, and moves training details and main-text ablations into appendices. Most existing methodological prose and the principal section sequence remain recognizable; much of the expansion is new scientific content.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from predominantly single-column to two-column formatting, substantially rearranging figures and tables. Tables 2 and 4 are transposed, the framework diagram's device label is corrected, and new result tables, a dynamic-throughput figure, and an FPAR histogram are added. Existing latency plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens deployment validation through large-model and downstream evaluations, quantization comparisons, non-ideal network tests, and accuracy uncertainty reporting. Explicit adaptation requirements and prefill limitations also improve interpretability. These gains outweigh lost repository-access and latency-run disclosures and some reporting errors: notably, Section 4.5 claims 5.13× over BP with Nb=4, whereas Table 7 supports about 2.97× at 10 Mbps; 5.13× corresponds to Nb=8.
